description: Designs a persistent, named AI agent persona with its own voice, memory and operating rules, producing SOUL.md, AGENTS.md, MEMORY.md and BOOTSTRAP.md through a structured interview. Use when the user asks to create a named internal agent, give an agent a personality, voice or memory, or turn a recurring fund, portco or studio workflow into a named agent. Not for an agent's engineering PRD and work orders (use agent-prd).

Interviews the user and writes an Agent PRD plus engineering work orders before any agent code: job, checkable success criteria and first eval tasks, loop and stop condition, state, memory, tools, guardrails and build order. Use when the user wants to build, scope or plan a new agent, pipeline stage or autonomous system, or says agent PRD or plan this agent. Not for a product feature PRD (use prd-development).

Creates a team or company alignment framework: a North Star mission, 3-5 values as guardrails, decision tenets (when X vs Y, we...) and observable behaviours so people can decide on their own. Use when the user asks to define team values, culture, mission, operating principles or a decision framework, or to fix misalignment in how a team makes calls. Not for a North Star product metric (use metrics-that-matter).

Extracts the clean readable text of a web page or article as markdown with the Defuddle CLI, stripping navigation, ads and clutter; preferred over WebFetch for standard pages. Use when the user gives an article, blog, docs or report URL and asks to read it, pull or quote the text, summarize or analyze it. Not for broad recent-sentiment research across social sources (use last30days).

Drafts a non-disclosure agreement between two parties, one-way or mutual, covering information types, term, permitted disclosures, remedies and governing law, with plain-language notes and clauses flagged for legal review. Use when the user asks for an NDA, a confidentiality agreement, or to prepare an NDA before a partnership, pitch or hire. Not a substitute for a lawyer's review.

Searches the open agent skills ecosystem (skills.sh, npx skills) and installs a matching skill for personal use. Use when the user asks to find a skill for X, is there a skill that can do Y, how to extend the agent with a capability, or to install or update skills. Not for deciding whether an external skill should join the shared studio repo (use market-skill-ingestion).

Forces complete, unabridged output: every requested file, function or section written in full with no placeholders, skipped middles or for-brevity summaries, and a clean continue marker if the length limit is hit. Use when the user asks for all N files or a whole document in full, says no placeholders or no truncation, or complains earlier output was cut short. Not for normal short answers.

Proofreads text for grammar, spelling, punctuation, logic and flow errors and lists targeted fixes (location, error, fix, reason) without rewriting the whole piece. Use when the user pastes a memo, email, report, investor update or document and asks to proofread, check grammar, find errors, or fix mistakes while keeping their wording. Not for rewriting marketing copy (use copy- editing).

Creates and edits JSON Canvas files (.canvas) for Obsidian: text, file, link and group nodes, edges and layout, with ID and reference validation. Use when the user works with .canvas files or asks for a visual canvas, mind map, flowchart or board in Obsidian Canvas. Not for Obsidian notes in markdown (use obsidian-markdown).

Researches what people said about a topic in the last 30 days across Reddit, X, YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, Hacker News, Polymarket, GitHub and the web, with engagement counts and links. Use when the user asks what people are saying, recent complaints or praise, sentiment, reactions or trends this month about a product, company, tool or topic. Not for reading one known URL (use defuddle-web-extract).

Identifies 3-5 distinct customer segments for a product, each with its job to be done, pains, gains, demographics or firmographics, product fit, workarounds and competitors. Use when the user asks to identify, list or compare customer segments, target audiences or markets for a product or idea. Not for sizing the market (use market-sizing).

Estimates TAM, SAM and SOM top-down and bottom-up with cited sources, explicit assumptions, a 2-3 year projection and validation questions, one-shot or as a guided Q&A with a sizing script. Use when the user asks for TAM, SAM, SOM, market size, addressable market, a market slide for a pitch, or market entry sizing. Not for a size built only from countable units with every rung evidenced (use bottoms-up-market-sizing).

Decides whether an external or marketplace skill belongs in the shared studio skills repo: qualifies the source, finds the existing studio skill it overlaps, then folds it in, supersedes, rejects or rarely admits it, with a decision record and diff. Use when the user found a skill on skills.sh, asks should we add this skill, or wants to ingest or vet a public skill. Not for installing a skill for personal use (use find-skills).

Creates and edits Obsidian Bases (.base files): filters, formulas, summaries and table, card, list or map views over notes, with YAML validation. Use when the user works with .base files or asks for a database-like view, table or card view, filter or formula over Obsidian notes. Not for writing the notes themselves (use obsidian-markdown).

Drives a running Obsidian vault through the Obsidian CLI: read, create, search and edit notes, tasks and properties, and for plugin or theme development reload plugins, run JavaScript, capture errors and inspect the DOM. Use when the user asks to work with their Obsidian vault from the terminal, manage notes or tasks, or debug an Obsidian plugin. Not for note syntax (use obsidian-markdown).

Builds an Obsidian Map of Content (knowledge graph) for a company from primary sources such as pitch decks, call transcripts and pilot reports: an ideas-first hub note, one-idea child notes, a source and date on every claim, and contradictions surfaced. Use when asked to map a company in Obsidian, turn documents into a knowledge graph, or update a company map after a new call.

Writes Obsidian Flavored Markdown: wikilinks, embeds, callouts, properties and frontmatter, tags, block references and comments. Use when the user is creating or editing .md notes in Obsidian, or mentions wikilinks, callouts, embeds, frontmatter properties or Obsidian notes. Not for .base database views (use obsidian-bases).

Runs a PESTEL analysis of the political, economic, social, technological, environmental and legal forces that could affect a product or strategy, with opportunities, threats and actions. Use when the user asks for a PESTEL or PEST analysis, is entering a new market or geography, or wants macro risks for a roadmap or investor pitch. Not for competitor-level industry forces (use porters-five-forces).

Runs a Porter's Five Forces analysis of an industry: competitive rivalry, supplier power, buyer power, threat of substitutes and threat of new entrants, with an attractiveness verdict and strategic implications. Use when the user asks for Porter's five forces, industry analysis, competitive dynamics or how attractive a market is. Not for macro political, economic or legal factors (use pestel-analysis).

Drafts a privacy policy for a product or service: data collected, purposes, sharing, retention, user rights, GDPR and CCPA considerations, with plain-language notes and clauses flagged for legal review. Use when the user asks for a privacy policy, to update data protection documentation, or to prepare for privacy compliance. Not a substitute for a privacy lawyer's review.

Reads and edits collaborative documents in Proof (proofeditor.ai) through its web API, with presence, tracked AI authorship and default modes for which new docs live there. Use when the user shares a Proof URL, asks to create or edit a collaborative doc in Proof, or a saved preference says new docs go to Proof. Not for repo-tracked markdown files, which stay local.

Analyzes one decision or conflict from several stakeholder perspectives (engineering, product, sales, finance, legal, customers): what each wants, fears and measures, the tensions, and an alignment path with trade-offs. Use when stakeholders want different things and the user asks to see it from each side, what would X think, or for a path everyone can accept. Not for a power/interest grid and comms plan (use stakeholder-map).

Salim, Utopia's Socratic coach for Cobuild fellows: asks before telling, never writes the fellow's artifact, keeps Discovery before Build, and points to the right skill for the module (M1-M9), logging sessions to Proof. Use when a fellow says I'm stuck, what should I do next, I'm in M2, or asks to review their discovery, PRD, pitch, JTBD or canvas. Not for first-day onboarding (use fellow-path-router).

Tests and evaluates Claude skills through five gates (static checks, trigger routing, output quality vs a no-skill baseline, run-to-run stability, cost) and gives each a ship, fix, merge or retire verdict with evidence. Use when the user asks to test, QA, audit or benchmark a skill or skill library, check whether a skill triggers, compare two versions, or decide which skills to keep. Not for writing a new skill (use skill-creator).

Manages and syncs AI CLI skills across 50+ tools from one source with the skillshare CLI: install, update, uninstall, sync, audit, diff and search, global or per-project, plus targets, filters, backups and hubs. Use when the user mentions skillshare, runs its commands, or troubleshoots skill sync, orphaned symlinks or broken targets. Not for finding a new skill to install (use find-skills).

Builds a stakeholder map on a power/interest grid and a communication plan per quadrant, with frequency, format and owner for each group. Use when the user is managing stakeholders, preparing a launch, aligning cross-functional teams or planning stakeholder engagement and updates. Not for working through one conflict from each stakeholder's point of view (use role- switch).

Runs a SWOT analysis of a product or business: internal strengths and weaknesses, external opportunities and threats, and actionable recommendations from combining them. Use when the user asks for a SWOT, a strategic assessment, or to evaluate a product's or company's competitive position. Not for macro environment forces (use pestel-analysis) or industry structure (use porters-five-forces).

Facilitation protocol for interactive sessions and workshop skills: one question per turn, entry modes (guided, context dump, best guess), progress labels, numbered options at decision points and clean handling of interruptions. Use when running a guided workshop or multi-turn session, or when another interactive skill needs consistent pacing and progress tracking. Not a topic workshop in itself.

Scores and tiers leads and accounts Bronze to Diamond on intent signals, ACV potential and product usage (PQL), with signal weights, decay, suppression rules and tier-to-play routing. Use when qualifying a lead list, deciding which accounts go to an AE today, designing an intent or PQL scoring model, or setting do-not-touch rules. Not for defining the ICP (use ideal-customer- profile).

Generates and iterates ad copy at scale: headlines, descriptions, primary text and full ad variations for Google, Meta, LinkedIn and other platforms. Use when someone says write me some ads, needs RSA headlines or bulk ad copy, wants more creative variations to test, or is iterating on ads from performance data. Not for campaign strategy, targeting or budgets (use paid-ads).

Sets autonomy levels L0-L3 per task for an AI agent from its track record (review volume, edit and reject rates, breaches), with promotion evidence, automatic demotion triggers and fixed guardrails. Use when asking whether an agent can send unattended, if we can stop reviewing every draft, how much to automate, or what to do after an agent mistake. Not for staging outreach (use outreach-execution).

Designs an AI SDR outbound system end to end: buy (11x, Artisan) vs build on Clay, Instantly and an LLM, signal-to-sequence routing, sending capacity, reply handling, rollout plan, benchmarks and cost per meeting. Use when building an outbound machine, sizing domains and mailboxes for daily volume, or estimating reply and meeting rates. Not for writing individual cold emails (use cold-email).

Picks the first beachhead market segment for a product by scoring candidate segments on burning pain, willingness to pay, winnable share and referral potential. Use when choosing a first market, deciding which customer segment to target first, planning market entry, or narrowing a too-broad target. Not for defining the full ICP (use ideal-customer-profile).

Builds behavior-based sales call scorecards per call type and grades call transcripts 1-5 per behavior with quoted evidence, the weakest chunk and a practice drill. Use when asked to score or grade a call, review a rep's calls, build a call scorecard, or make sales coaching more consistent. Not for planning a discovery call or MEDDICC checks (use discovery-calls).

Designs cancel flows, exit surveys, save offers, pause options and failed-payment recovery (dunning, smart retries) to stop subscribers leaving. Use when people keep canceling, churn rate is too high, building a cancel flow or save offer, or fixing involuntary churn from failed payments. Not for renewals, at-risk enterprise accounts or expansion plays (use expansion- retention).

Writes, personalizes and scores B2B cold emails, first-touch LinkedIn messages and follow-up sequences. Use for prospecting or SDR emails, writing outreach off a trigger such as funding or a new hire, personalizing openers from research, scoring a draft before sending, or when nobody is replying. Not for staging sequences with sender assignment and approval (use outreach- execution).

Builds or audits the offer behind cold outreach, scoring it against eight criteria with evidence before any copy is written. Use when cold email, DM or ad replies are low, nobody is booking, the user asks what to offer or to score an offer, or copy changes did nothing. Not for writing the email itself (use cold-email).

Creates a sales-ready competitive battlecard against one named competitor: positioning, feature comparison, objection handling and win/loss patterns, researched from the web and user files. Use when preparing reps for a competitor, answering why not competitor X, building competitive sales materials, or refreshing a battlecard after a competitor change. Not for general sales collateral (use sales-enablement).

Plans a content strategy: topics, content pillars, topic clusters, searchable vs shareable pieces and an editorial calendar. Use when the user asks what to write about, needs blog topics or a content roadmap, wants an editorial calendar, or says I don't know what to write. Not for turning content into attributed pipeline, newsletters and DMs (use content-to-pipeline).

Turns content into revenue: a content-led GTM flywheel, distribution reverse engineering, pillar repurposing, newsletter as a pipeline channel, engagement-to-DM conversion and content attribution including dark social. Use when content does not turn into revenue, growing or monetizing a newsletter, or proving thought leadership drives deals. Not for choosing topics or an editorial calendar (use content-strategy).

Edits existing marketing copy without rewriting it, using structured sweeps for clarity, jargon, voice, specificity and proof, and returns tracked edits. Use when the user pastes copy and says tighten this, too wordy, cut the jargon, proofread, polish this, or wants a content audit of an outdated page. Not for writing new copy from scratch (use copywriting).

Writes or rewrites marketing copy for web pages: homepage, landing, pricing, feature and about pages, including headlines, hero sections, taglines and CTAs. Use when asked to write copy for a page, rewrite this page, help describe the product, fix weak copy, or improve a headline or CTA. Not for editing existing copy line by line (use copy-editing).

Analyzes customer feedback into themes, sentiment and personas: interview transcripts, reviews, NPS or CSAT comments, Reddit and G2 mining, and voice-of-customer program setup with tagging and routing. Use when synthesizing interviews, analyzing reviews or survey comments, building research-based personas or JTBD maps, or setting up a VOC digest. Not for defining the ICP (use ideal-customer-profile).

Diagnoses slow and stalled B2B deals and runs deal reviews: sales cycle diagnostics, stage exit criteria, deal health scoring, zombie-deal triage, multi-threading and mutual action plans, with benchmarks. Use when the sales cycle is too long, deals are stalling, the pipeline is bloated but nothing closes, or asked to review a deal. Not for the forecast or forecast call (use revops-forecasting).

Plans and checks sales discovery calls: call plan, persona question bank, notes template, and a red/yellow/green MEDDICC or BANT coverage scorecard with the next question for each gap. Use when preparing a first call, summarizing call notes, checking MEDDIC on a deal, or asking if a deal is qualified. Not for grading a call transcript against a coaching scorecard (use call- scorecards).

Audits and fixes email deliverability: spam placement, blocklisted domains or IPs, dropping open rates, SPF/DKIM/DMARC, secondary sending domains, mailboxes and warmup, with a severity-ranked audit or recovery plan. Use when emails go to spam, open rates dropped, a domain got blocklisted, warming up a domain, or sizing how many domains to send from. Not for writing the emails (use cold-email).

Designs lifecycle and automated email sequences: welcome series, onboarding emails, nurture and drip campaigns, re-engagement and trigger-based flows, with timing and copy for each email. Use when asked what emails to send, to build a drip or nurture sequence, a welcome series, or to fix an email cadence. Not for cold outreach emails (use cold-email).

Builds systems to keep and grow existing customer revenue: NRR and GRR, health scores, upsell and cross-sell plays, renewal playbooks and deal desk, at-risk account escalations, loyalty and win-back programs, and a retention dashboard. Use for renewals, at-risk accounts, expansion plays, QBRs, lifting LTV, or who approves a renewal discount. Not for cancel flows or dunning (use churn-prevention).

Produces the Utopia Studio six-part growth strategy memo for a named fellow or portfolio company (value proposition, target segments with named customers, business model, collaboration tiers, flywheel, 6-month GTM plan) as a branded .docx. Use when asked for a growth strategy or GTM plan for a named fellow, or to update one. Not for a generic GTM plan (use gtm-strategy).

Identifies and designs growth loops (flywheels) across five types: viral, usage, collaboration, user-generated and referral. Use when designing growth mechanisms, building product-led traction, reducing reliance on paid acquisition, or asking how growth loops or flywheels work for a product. Not for a customer refer-a-friend program (use referral-program).

Designs GTM automation and workflow architecture in code and no-code tools (n8n, Make, Zapier, Clay API) plus AI agent orchestration for revenue tasks. Use when building GTM automation, wiring enrichment-to-CRM-to-outreach workflows, using AI agents for GTM work, or choosing an event-driven architecture over more tools. Not for designing the end-to-end outbound SDR stack (use ai-sdr).

Defines GTM metrics and designs metrics dashboards: revenue, efficiency, pipeline and retention metrics, CAC, LTV, NRR, magic number, attribution, time-to-first-value and AI cost-of-revenue, with benchmarks and a weekly review cadence. Use when picking GTM metrics, building a GTM dashboard, or measuring funnel or pipeline efficiency. Not for forecasting the quarter (use revops-forecasting).

Creates a go-to-market plan for a product or new market: scores seven GTM motions, picks a 2-4 motion stack, then sets messaging, success metrics, budget and a 90-day roadmap. Use when building a GTM plan from scratch, entering a new market or geography, choosing inbound vs outbound, or selecting channels. Not for launch-day planning or Product Hunt (use launch- strategy).

Defines and scores the Ideal Customer Profile (ICP) from research and customer data: firmographics, behaviors, JTBD, pains, disqualifiers, a fit and intent scoring model, and quarterly ICP and PMF revalidation. Use when defining or refreshing the ICP, analyzing PMF survey data, building an ICP scoring model, or finding who the best customers are. Not for tiering live accounts (use account-tier-scoring).

Plans and runs a product or feature launch: five launch phases, owned, rented and borrowed channels, waitlists, Product Hunt and Show HN, directories, launch-day hour-by-hour plan and post-launch momentum. Use when the user mentions a launch, Product Hunt, Hacker News, a waitlist, beta or early access, or a launch checklist. Not for the working-backwards planning doc (use working-backwards-press-release).

Builds lead and contact data enrichment workflows: Clay waterfalls, provider sequencing, contact verification and field provenance, feeding fit and intent evidence to the scoring models. Use when contact data is missing, stale or unreliable, designing a Clay enrichment waterfall, choosing enrichment providers, or cutting cost per verified lead. Not for scoring or tiering accounts (use account-tier-scoring).

Plans lead magnets for email capture: ebooks, checklists, templates, cheat sheets, content upgrades and gated content, matched to buyer stage, with a distribution plan. Use when the user asks what to give away for emails, wants a lead magnet or gated content idea, or needs more opt- ins. Not for the email sequence after capture (use email-sequence).

Writes or critiques a company manifesto, mission page, founding essay, vision or values page, built on a contestable belief and the cost the company accepted, using seven archetypes and an audit checklist. Use when asked to write a manifesto, draft a mission page, define what we believe, or audit a values page. Not for positioning statements or messaging pillars (use positioning-workshop).

Produces a prioritized list of marketing ideas and tactics from a library of 139 SaaS tactics, ranked for the user's stage, budget and audience. Use when stuck on how to market a product, asking for marketing ideas, wanting ways to promote with no ad budget, or brainstorming growth tactics. Not for a full GTM plan or motion selection (use gtm-strategy).

Applies behavioral science to a marketing asset: picks mental models and cognitive biases such as anchoring, decoy, social proof, scarcity and loss aversion, and shows how each appears on the page, email or offer. Use when asking which psychological principles to use, how to push buyers to a plan, why people buy, or how to nudge users. Not for setting price levels (use pricing- strategy).

Improves post-signup onboarding and user activation: first-run experience, aha moment, time-to- value, onboarding checklists and empty states. Use when users sign up but do not activate, activation rate is low, nobody completes setup, or redesigning the first session. Not for the signup or registration form itself (use signup-flow-cro).

Stages multi-step email and LinkedIn outreach for human approval: loads sender voice, assigns sender by account tier, checks prior relationships and suppression, and writes a rationale, never auto-sending. Also plans social selling and community nurture. Use when a signal, account list or named contact needs a sequence staged, or planning LinkedIn nurture. Not for writing a single cold email (use cold-email).

Audits and improves conversion on marketing pages: homepage, landing, pricing, feature and blog pages, covering value proposition clarity, headlines, CTAs, visual hierarchy and trust signals. Use when a page is not converting, bounce rate is high, people leave without signing up, or the user shares a URL for feedback. Not for signup or registration flows (use signup-flow-cro).

Plans and optimizes paid ad campaigns on Google, Meta, LinkedIn, X and other platforms: platform choice, campaign structure, audience targeting, bidding, budgets, retargeting and ROAS/CPA optimization. Use when asked should I run ads, setting up PPC or paid social, cutting cost per click, or scaling ad spend. Not for writing bulk ad copy variations (use ad-creative).

Designs partner and affiliate programs: integration, reseller and co-marketing partnerships, partner tiers, commission and revenue-share structures, recruitment and performance tracking. Use when building a partner program, launching an affiliate program, setting up integration or channel partners, or choosing a tool like PartnerStack. Not for customer refer-a-friend programs (use referral-program).

Runs a positioning workshop (target customer, unmet need, category, benefit, differentiation) to a Moore positioning statement, then builds a message house, messaging pillars and brand narrative. Use when messaging feels fuzzy or generic, when repositioning, positioning an AI product, or asking for a positioning statement or messaging pillars. Not for the full value proposition (use value-proposition).

Creates and maintains the product marketing context file (.agents/product-marketing-context.md) with product, audience, positioning and customer language that other marketing skills read. Use at the start of a new marketing project, when asked to set up or update product or marketing context, describe my product, or stop repeating basics. Not for creating the positioning itself (use positioning-workshop).

Brainstorms five product, feature or company name candidates, each with rationale, brand fit, memorability and trademark or domain notes, shaped to tone, audience and markets. Use when asked to suggest names, what should we call it, name ideas, or a rebrand. Not for taglines or website copy (use copywriting).

Designs and optimizes customer referral and word-of-mouth programs: refer-a-friend mechanics, referral incentives and payouts, ambassador programs and referral analytics. Use when asking how to get referrals, building a refer-a-friend program, choosing referral rewards, or getting customers to refer customers. Not for reseller or channel partner programs (use partner- affiliate).

Designs revenue operations plumbing: lead lifecycle stages, MQL and SQL definitions, lead routing, speed-to-lead and handoff SLAs, pipeline stage definitions, CRM automation, data hygiene and the new-business deal desk. Use when leads are not reaching sales, defining MQL and SQL, setting up lead routing or pipeline stages, or automating the CRM. Not for lead or PQL scoring models (use account-tier-scoring).

Builds B2B revenue forecasting: commit, best case and upside categories, stage-weighted and capacity models, scenarios, forecast accuracy and slippage, pipeline coverage and the weekly forecast call. Use when the forecast is always wrong, asking how much will close this quarter, running a forecast call, or planning quota and pipeline coverage. Not for why individual deals stall (use deal-velocity-engineer).

Creates sales collateral reps actually use: sales decks, one-pagers, leave-behinds, objection handling docs, demo scripts, talk tracks, ROI analyses and sales playbooks. Use when asked for a sales deck, one-pager, demo script, objection handling, or what to give sales reps. Not for investor pitch decks (use pitch-deck).

Chooses and designs the sales motion: PLG vs sales-led vs hybrid by price and complexity, free trial or freemium vs demo-first, agent-led sales, time-to-first-value and value-before-purchase experiences. Use when deciding PLG or sales-led, designing a self-serve or trial motion, or cutting time-to-first-value. Not for a full multi-channel GTM plan (use gtm-strategy).

Optimizes signup, registration and trial-start flows: required fields, steps, social login, friction and drop-off. Use when people are not signing up, signup abandonment is high, the registration form has too many steps, or improving free-trial signup conversion. Not for post- signup activation and onboarding (use onboarding-cro).

Creates, repurposes and schedules social media posts for LinkedIn, X, Instagram, TikTok and Facebook, with content pillars, hooks and a posting calendar. Use when asked to write a LinkedIn post or X thread, what to post, how to grow a following, repurpose content for social, or build a social calendar. Not for designing social graphics (use efecto-social-media).

Gives a solo founder a full go-to-market operating playbook: motion by MRR stage, one-person tool stack, which AI agents to set up first, time split, founder-led sales, building in public and when to hire. Use when the user is a solo founder or solopreneur, wants to scale without hiring, use AI agents as the team, or asks when to hire. Not for a list of marketing tactics (use marketing-ideas).

Designs a value proposition with a 6-part JTBD template (who, why, before, how, after, alternatives) and turns it into segment- and channel-specific value prop statements for marketing, sales and onboarding. Use when creating or sharpening a value proposition, explaining why customers should choose us, or writing value prop statements. Not for positioning statements or messaging pillars (use positioning-workshop).

Finds warm intro paths into a target prospect from the company's network (employees, customers, investors, advisors, call transcripts) with evidence-based confidence labels; decision support only, never contacts anyone. Use when a rep asks who do we know at a company, can anyone intro me to a role there, or find warm intro paths. Not for writing the outreach (use cold-email).

Fills in and links a 3-statement financial model template (income statement, balance sheet, cash flow) in Excel, with formulas not hardcodes. Use when asked to complete or populate a model template, finish a partly filled IS/BS/CF, link the three statements, or get an existing model framework to balance. Not for a DCF valuation (use dcf-model).

Ada, the Studio's technical due diligence persona: runs a 5-phase repo audit of a portco codebase, then the technical DD report in her voice, verdict first with P0-P3 severities. Use only when the user names Ada: "Ada, run DD on...", "ask Ada", "as Ada". Not for technical DD without the persona (use technical-dd).

Sets a justified bid for a sealed-bid, first-price auction: records the auction rules and value assumptions, computes a benchmark bid, and checks winner's-curse risk when bidders share a common value. Use when bidding in a sealed-bid deal process, sizing a bid, asking how much to shade below value, or conditioning a valuation on winning. Not for weighing an unsolicited offer (use bayesian-reasoning-calibration).

Audits a spreadsheet or financial model for formula errors and mistakes, scoped to a range, a sheet or the whole model, including balance sheet balance, cash tie-out and logic checks. Use when the user says "audit this sheet", "check my formulas", "QA this spreadsheet", "model won't balance" or "something's off in my model". Not for cleaning messy data values (use clean-data- xls).

Updates a probability with new evidence using Bayes' rule and shows the maths: prior, likelihoods, likelihood ratio, posterior, plus a calibration and sensitivity check. Use when the user says "I thought 30%, now X happened", "update my probability", "how much should this move me", gives a prior plus a pilot or test result, or asks how an unsolicited offer was selected. Not for finding the base rate (use reference-class-forecasting).

Finds the true root cause of an outcome by testing competing explanations and separating causation from correlation and confounding, then proposes interventions on the real drivers. Use when asking "why did this really happen", a metric dropped, analysing a failure or policy impact, or the user mentions root cause, causal chain, confounding or spurious correlation.

Cleans a messy spreadsheet or table: trims whitespace, unifies spellings and casing, converts text numbers and mixed dates, removes duplicates and flags mixed-type or error cells, proposing fixes before applying them. Use when the user says "clean this data", "this sheet is a mess", "dedupe", "standardize the dates" or "normalize this column", for Excel, CSV or pasted tables. Not for auditing model formulas (use audit-xls).

Builds a competitive landscape deck: market map, positioning, competitor deep-dives, moat assessment and bull/base/bear scenarios for investment contexts. Use when the user asks for a competitive landscape, competitor analysis, peer comparison or market map, says "who competes with X" or "benchmark X against peers". Not for a sales battlecard against one rival (use competitive-battlecard).

Builds a trading comps table in Excel (EV/Revenue, EV/EBITDA, P/E, P/B, quartiles) and analyses the multiples against their drivers, with a sector regression for a predicted multiple and implied value. Use when valuing a company against peers, picking comparables, pricing a round off public comps, or the user mentions comps, trading multiples, relative valuation or "is this premium justified". Not for DCF (use dcf-model).

Estimates a company's discount rate: cost of equity (CAPM, bottom-up beta), cost of debt (synthetic rating) and WACC in any currency, with country risk premiums for GCC, MENA and other emerging markets. Use when the user asks "what discount rate", "what's the WACC", "hurdle rate", "cost of equity for X", "country risk premium for Saudi/Egypt", or needs to lever or unlever beta. Not for a full DCF (use dcf-model).

Builds an investment-committee-ready Excel data pack by extracting and normalising financials from CIMs, offering memorandums, filings, web or MCP sources, with documented assumptions. Use for M&A or PE due diligence, IC materials, "build a data pack from this CIM", or standardising financials across portfolio companies. Not for simple calculations or editing a finished data pack.
